findings.message: This fence carries no language, so it renders unhighlighted and nothing says whether that was intended.
findings.consequence: An unlabelled fence renders unhighlighted and nothing on the page says whether that was intended, so a typo in the language name looks exactly like a deliberate plain block. Fences that really are not code take the plain language, which is the member that exists for them.
findings.remediation: Label it. Use "text" for output, a tree or anything that is deliberately not code.

findings.message: The prose uses U+2013 en dash as punctuation.
findings.consequence: It reads as an em dash to everyone but a typesetter, and it is the same house rule. Between digits it is correct and permitted, because rewriting a numeric range is not an improvement.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the sentence with a comma or a colon. Between two digits the character is correct and this rule permits it.

findings.message: The wording "seamless" is on the house banned list.
findings.consequence: Each phrase on the list is one a reader has met a thousand times in generated copy, and one of them on a page is enough for the whole page to read as machine written. The list is a hard rule, which is why a project may add to it and may not remove from it.
findings.remediation: It claims an absence of friction the reader will discover for themselves, and it is the word most often used to cover a step the page has not documented.
findings.excerpt: ...ross. Passing a payload between them is seamless because both sides already speak , so t...

findings.message: The prose uses U+2014 em dash as punctuation.
findings.consequence: The em dash is the single most reliable marker of copy nobody read back, and this is one of the estate house rules, stated as a hard rule rather than a preference. That is why a project may raise it and may not lower it.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the sentence with a comma, a colon, brackets, or two sentences.

findings.message: The prose uses U+2192 rightwards arrow as punctuation.
findings.consequence: A screen reader announces the character by name in every one of the seven languages, and a search for the word the character was standing in for matches nothing. A glyph that is really data is recognised as a status node before this rule runs, so what it sees is decoration.
findings.remediation: Write the word the character was standing in for. A glyph that carries data belongs in a table cell, where the compiler reads it as a status.

findings.message: The text here matches the deny list pattern "station-pack".
findings.consequence: This is the rule that stands between an internal tree name, an export-compliance note or a device identifier and a public mirror. It is protected for the same reason the public sync script dies on any hit: a scan that examined nothing has cleared nothing.
findings.remediation: Names an internal test fixture directory. Publishing the name tells a reader a tree exists and what to ask for.

findings.message: "Contoso Tap" is on the deny list and this page is published.
findings.consequence: The names come from the deny list, which lives outside the publishable root because it is the list of things that must not ship. A competitor named on a public page is a comparison the company has to stand behind, made by whoever wrote that sentence.
findings.remediation: Describe the behaviour without naming the product. A comparison on a public page is one the company has to stand behind.
findings.excerpt: Contoso Tap keeps its codec inside the app target,...

findings.message: The ar translation of "guide/first-tag" is older than its source.
findings.consequence: A stale translation describes behaviour the app no longer has, and it carries no sign of that on the page. It is worse than a missing translation, which at least tells the reader what they are looking at.
findings.remediation: Retranslate it. Staleness comes from git committer dates rather than from a field, so there is nothing to refresh but the text.

findings.message: "developer/architecture" has no zh translation.
findings.consequence: Under graceful parity the site serves the source text with a notice and no indexing, which is a reader in one of seven languages reading English. Under required parity the same state blocks the publish, which is what the mode is for.
findings.remediation: Write content/zh/developer/architecture.md, or accept the fallback: under graceful parity the site serves the source locale with a notice and noindex.
